    How to Use the Yes or No Decision Maker

    Type your question, or don't, and tap Decide. You get Yes, No or Maybe, with your question shown above the answer so a screenshot makes sense later. Decide again asks again, and the last 10 answers are listed underneath.

    The odds

    Out of the box it's 45% Yes, 45% No and 10% Maybe. Open Change the odds to set your own. The numbers are shares, not a strict percentage, so 2 / 1 / 0 means Yes comes up twice as often as No and Maybe never does. The page shows the actual chances as you type.

    The answer is picked with your browser's secure random number generator, not the predictable kind built into most simple scripts. Your question isn't sent anywhere or saved. It doesn't even affect the answer: the tool doesn't read it, it just shows it back to you.

    Ways to use it

    • Dinner. "Should we get takeout?"
    • Friendly arguments. Agree to abide by it before you ask.
    • Movie night. "Do we watch the long one?"
    • Breaking a tie. When the vote is split down the middle.
    • Classroom games. Quick yes-or-no rounds, with Maybe set to 0.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Is it really random?

    Yes. The answer is picked with your browser's secure random number generator, using the odds you see on the page: 45% Yes, 45% No and 10% Maybe unless you change them.

    Can I change the odds?

    Yes. Open Change the odds and set a weight from 0 to 100 for each answer. They don't have to add up to 100. 50 / 50 / 0 gives a straight yes or no.

    What does Maybe mean?

    It means the tool isn't going to make this one for you. Ask again, or set Maybe to 0 if you want a firm answer every time.

    Can I ask a question?

    Yes. Type it in and it's shown above the answer, which is handy for screenshots. The question doesn't change the odds.

    Is my question uploaded anywhere?

    No. Everything stays in your browser. The question isn't sent anywhere or saved, and the history clears when you close the tab.
